transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because the doctor who did my insurance physical said my weight was too low. I don't really agree, honestly. To me, I just look lean from being up on ladders and working long days painting. But they told me I needed to come in and see someone about it, so... that's why I'm here.
How would you feel if you were to gain some weight?

Honestly, I wouldn't like it. If the scale goes up even a little bit—like if I have a dinner with a client or eat something with bread—I get pretty tense about it. I usually start cutting back the next day just to make sure it doesn't stick. So, yeah, the idea of gaining weight isn't something I'm comfortable with.
When you look at yourself, do you feel that you are overweight or that parts of your body are too fat?

I wouldn't say I feel overweight overall, but... yeah, certain parts definitely bother me. Like, when I catch myself in a mirror, or... you know, if I see a photo of myself standing next to one of my murals. I basically judge my whole day by whether my stomach and my face look sharp enough. If they don't, if they look soft at all, then yeah, I definitely feel like there's too much fat there.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, such as periods becoming irregular or stopping completely?
Uh, well... I'm a guy, so no. I don't have a menstrual cycle. That doesn't really apply to me.
Have you noticed any decrease in your sex drive or difficulties with sexual performance?
Uh, no, not really. I haven't noticed any changes with that. Everything seems pretty normal in that department, to be honest.
